chunks: My father narrated to me from ʿAbd Allah ibn Jamil ibn ʿAyyash, Abū ʿAlī al-Bazzāz, who said: My father informed me, saying:

I asked Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام about a garment made by the People of the Book: may I perform salat (prayer) in it before it is washed? He said, “There is no harm, though that it be washed is more beloved to me.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Salat (prayer) is not permissible in privies, or houses of fires, and houses of wines, or on the main parts of roads, or in the resting places of camels, or on saline ground.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْكِتَابِ: the People of the Book, referring to scriptural religious communities
key_terms.الثَّوْبِ: a garment or clothing used for salat (prayer)
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer in Islam
key_terms.جَوَادِّ الطُّرُقِ: the main thoroughfares or traveled parts of roads
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or legal objection
key_terms.مَعَاطِنِ الْإِبِلِ: the resting or watering places of camels
key_terms.يُغْسَلَ: to be washed, indicating a preferred act of purification

ai.seo_question: Can one perform salat (prayer) in clothes made by the People of the Book, and where is salat (prayer) not permissible?
ai.summary: This report addresses rulings related to salat (prayer) garments and places of prayer. It states that a garment made by the People of the Book may be used for salat (prayer) before washing, although washing it is preferred, and it also lists places in which salat (prayer) is not valid.
